title: fix(app-shell): Studio Interfaces item header names a label-less object entry by its label, as the rail does
body:

_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8LSNZTBKB5UepDXQ6qob588)_
Fixes #26746

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:Studio「界面」条目标题(标题、读屏说明、定义抽屉标题)改为与左侧导航行同一套标签解析,每次渲染现解析。
- 为什么改:无标签的对象导航项(脚手架生成的就是这种)标题显示机器名 `repairs_ticket`,而侧栏已显示「Repair Ticket」。
- 风险与回滚:仅 app-shell 一个私有包、一个文件的显示文本;回滚即 revert 本 PR,无数据或契约变化。
- 先看:`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` 中新增的 `ifTitleText` 一段;其次新测试文件 `StudioDesignSurface.itemHeaderLabel-26746.test.tsx`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.itemHeaderLabel-26746.test.tsx`,预期 3 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

The Interfaces item header read `current.label || current.name` in three places: the header title, its screen-reader caption beside the kind chip, and the definition sheet's title (`engine.studio.if.definitionTitle`). `current.label` is the open leaf's display text frozen when its Surface was made. On the first load that happens before the resolver knows every label. For example, a draft-only object's `_drafts` row lands after the app load picks its first leaf. The rail asks the resolver again on every render, so it read "Repair Ticket" while the header kept "repairs_ticket · Object".

The three sites now read one value, `ifTitleText`. It finds the open leaf's entry in `railTree` (the tree the rail draws, served text included) by `navId` and names it through the rail's own `navEntryLabelText` with the same `useNavTargetLabel` resolver. No second resolver is added. A Surface without a `navId` keeps `current.label`, and an empty text keeps the existing `current.name` fallback.

## Why

The rail and the header name the same leaf, and the label wins over the machine name everywhere (ruling B of objectui#11201, the `navEntryLabelText` contract). Triage 6448317687: "Resolve the object label the way the rail does."

## Tests

New `StudioDesignSurface.itemHeaderLabel-26746.test.tsx` mounts the whole surface and holds the `_drafts` answer until the header has opened on its first leaf:

- a label-less object entry: the header, its caption and its tooltip read "Repair Ticket" once the label arrives, with the machine name only on the tooltip;
- a labelled entry: the header reads its authored label, unchanged;
- a label-less group: the rail's group header reads what the runtime sidebar's `resolveNavItemLabel` gives it, and a leaf inside it is named alike in the rail and the header.

Ablation, after the fix was committed: `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the resolver line with `const text = current.label;` (the old `current.label || current.name`). Tests 1 and 3 went red with `Received: repairs_ticket · Object`, the QA symptom; test 2 stayed green. The restore leg was verified by blob: HEAD and disk both `d05fa2404f2a`, `git diff HEAD` empty. The test imports the surface by relative path, so there is no dist leg.

## Acceptance notes

- Label-less groups: the rail shows a label-less group's `id` (for example `nav_item_2`, drawn uppercase by the rail group style). This is the runtime's own rule: `resolveNavItemLabel` in `@object-ui/layout` falls to the entry `id` for a group, and the running app's sidebar shows the same text. The header never names a group, because a group is not a Surface. So the rail and the header already agree, and `NavTreeGroup` is unchanged. Test 3 pins that the rail matches the runtime. Giving label-less groups a different text would be a change to the runtime rule, not to this header.
- Outside this card's surface, the same frozen-label read remains in two places, reported only: the Automation pillar header's `current.label || current.name`, and the `onSurfaceLabelChange` report to the dock, which reads `current.label`.
